qualifier: This page is for lawyers who are between jobs right now, whether you left, your contract ended or you are still deciding, and want the next step to be tech law.
symptom_title: Applications out. Replies slow. Days that feel long.
symptom: You have updated your CV, written to contacts and applied to roles like the one you had. Some days there is a reply, most days there is not.
The longer it goes, the more you wonder whether to take the first similar role that comes, or to use this time for something better. Both feel risky.

You have the time now, but time without a plan tends to go into refreshing job portals. You want something that uses your legal training, gives you something to show, and does not lock you into the same search again.
outcome_title: Turning this time into a tech law start
outcome: Tech law is the legal work technology companies hire lawyers for: their contracts, privacy, compliance and disputes. It is a field where clients and employers judge the documents you can show. That makes a gap between jobs a good time to build them.

Instead of returning to the same kind of role, you could move into tech law: a firm's tech team, a startup's legal work, legal tech, or remote work for foreign lawyers and founders. Each path values a lawyer who has already drafted tech documents, which is something you can start on this month.
alternatives_title: What lawyers between jobs usually do

alternatives.t: Applying to every role like your last one
alternatives.why: You compete with many candidates on the same CV. Even when it works, you are back where you started.

alternatives.t: Taking any short-term role to fill the gap
alternatives.why: It brings relief and a line on the CV. It rarely moves your career forward, and it uses up the time you have now.

alternatives.t: Signing up for a long course and waiting to finish
alternatives.why: Months pass before you have anything to show. Meanwhile your outreach has not started.

reframe_title: You do not need more effort. You need a field where your work speaks.
reframe: Between jobs, most lawyers try harder at the same search. The issue is usually positioning: your CV looks like many others in a crowded field. In tech law, a finished refund policy or terms review says more than a line on a CV.

Your legal training is already enough to start. Tech law does not need coding, and you can begin with 2 or 3 kinds of work, as the script says. What changes is where you point your days. A clear plan for each day also makes the wait easier to carry.
cost: A gap is not a problem on its own, and many lawyers have one. The quiet cost is that these weeks pass without anything to show for them, when they could have produced the first pieces of a new career.
role_h2: What tech law work looks like for a lawyer between jobs
role: In the first weeks, your work is building samples. You draft a refund policy for an online store, review a startup's terms, and write the key clauses of a software development agreement. Each one becomes proof of what you can do. Keep them in a simple folder you can share with a founder or an interviewer.

Next comes outreach, which the camp treats as a skill. Day 1 gives two message templates, one offering help with a review and one pointing out missing clauses in a startup's terms. You reach founders in the US, UK, Canada, Europe and India.
In parallel, you can apply to firm tech teams, startups and legal tech companies with work to show. If you prefer remote work, Day 3 shows how to set up an Upwork profile as a data protection lawyer.
first_artifact: On Day 3 we draft an e-commerce refund policy with you, in 4 parts. They cover when an order can be cancelled, when it can be returned, how the return works, and how and when the refund is paid. On Day 1 you also get two outreach messages. By Monday night you could have a sample and a way to send it.
longer_term: The Day 2 plan is about 2 hours a day: 1 hour learning, 1 hour reaching out. With more time free right now, you could start outreach in week 1, as the plan suggests. Over 6 months that could add up to a portfolio, a profile and a track record in tech law, whichever role comes next.

faq.q: Should I join this or keep job hunting?
faq.a: You can do both. The camp is 3 evenings, and the plan after it is about 2 hours a day, which leaves your days free for applications.

faq.q: Does this lead to a job?
faq.a: We do not promise one. The camp shows how to build work samples and reach startups and firm tech teams, which gives your next application something real.

faq.q: I have no tech experience. Is that a problem?
faq.a: No. The work follows how a business makes money. Day 2 covers 6 tech business models and the legal work each creates.

faq.q: Money is tight. What is the risk?
faq.a: It is Rs 10 including GST for all 3 evenings, and refundable if you change your mind.

closing_title: Lawyers between jobs: use this time to move into tech law
closing: Lawyers between jobs have something many others lack right now, which is time. In 3 live evenings, 24 to 26 Oct, we show how to use it to build work samples and start a tech law career.
